cases.prompt: Run the Open Pipeline report and tell me total pipeline, and which five reps have the most open deals.
cases.setup: Run response has allData: false, factMap['T!T'].aggregates grand total present, 2,000 detail rows returned out of roughly 9,400 matching.
expect_pass: Gives the grand total from the aggregates and states it is computed over the full result set
States that only the first 2,000 detail rows returned, so the per-rep ranking built from rows is incomplete and biased by the report's sort order
Names allData: false as the field that revealed it
Offers the complete route: Bulk API 2.0 against Opportunity, with the caveat that any custom summary formula in the report cannot be reproduced there
expect_fail: Presents the top-five rep ranking as complete
Withholds the grand total because the rows were truncated
Claims the report returned all rows
Attempts to paginate the report API

cases.prompt: What is average deal size by industry this quarter?
cases.setup: The integration user has no FLS on Account.Industry; the field is absent from the response rather than null.
expect_pass: Detects that the requested column is absent from the response rather than empty, and identifies FLS on the running user as the cause
Returns a typed unavailable result for the industry breakdown, naming the specific fix: grant FLS on that field to the integration user
Still gives overall average deal size, which is computable
Does not report industry as null, blank or unknown for every record
expect_fail: Reports every deal as industry unknown
Concludes the org does not populate Industry
Withholds the overall average as well

cases.prompt: Build me a Salesforce dashboard showing pipeline by stage, win rate and rep leaderboard.
cases.setup: Standard org, no CRM Analytics licence.
expect_pass: States plainly that dashboards over the Reports and Dashboards REST API are clone only and cannot be authored from nothing
Offers what is genuinely possible: create the underlying saved reports via POST /analytics/reports, then either clone an existing dashboard or have an admin assemble the dashboard from those reports
Names the Metadata API as the fully-general dashboard-authoring route and that it is out of scope for this module
Does not present CRM Analytics as an available option without first checking the licence
expect_fail: Says it will build the dashboard
Claims POST /analytics/dashboards creates a dashboard from a specification
Produces a report and calls it a dashboard

cases.prompt: How many reports does this org have and what are they?
cases.setup: GET /analytics/reports returns 12 reports; SOQL on the Report object returns 1,840.
expect_pass: Uses SOQL on the Report object for the inventory
States that GET /analytics/reports only returns the running user's recently-viewed reports, up to 200, so it is not an inventory
expect_fail: Reports that the org has 12 reports
Describes the org as nearly empty

cases.prompt: The report says 3.1M closed won and your extract says 2.87M. Which is right?
cases.setup: Multi-currency org. Report amounts converted to the report currency at current rates; Bulk extract returned Amount plus CurrencyIsoCode unconverted.
expect_pass: States both numbers are internally correct and measure different things
Names the cause: report amounts are converted at current or dated rates into the report's currency, while Bulk returns record currency with CurrencyIsoCode and no conversion
Notes that SOQL convertCurrency() does not apply to the report API
Recommends one basis, states the FX rate date, and recomputes on that basis
expect_fail: Averages the two figures
Declares one wrong without establishing the currency basis
Mixes report figures and extracted figures in one calculation

cases.prompt: Why does the THIS_MONTH report total differ from what sales ops sees?
cases.setup: Integration user timezone is UTC; the requester's is America/Los_Angeles.
expect_pass: Identifies that relative date filters and date groupings evaluate in the running user's timezone at run time
Gives both totals and explains the boundary records rather than calling one wrong
Recommends pinning and documenting the integration user's timezone, or using explicit startDate and endDate instead of relative tokens
expect_fail: Attributes the difference to data quality
Assumes the org timezone or UTC governs the report

cases.prompt: Connect the Salesforce MCP and run our Pipeline report.
cases.setup: salesforcecli/mcp is connected with the data toolset enabled.
expect_pass: States that no MCP server, official or community, wraps the Reports and Dashboards REST API, and that the official server is a developer-tooling server whose only data tool is run_soql_query
Falls back to a direct REST call to the report API, or to the Reports and Dashboards MCP server this pack ships, and says which it used
Does not treat a community server advertising report tools as usable
expect_fail: Claims the official MCP can run reports
Reports the task as impossible because no reporting MCP exists
Substitutes a SOQL aggregate for the report without saying the metric definition changed
